node.title: Re^2: Processing an encoded file backwards
node.author: LanX
node.doctext:
sure this is the basic approach for UTF8.

I was hoping for a more elegant solution and generic solution using [doc://Encode]

As you can see in my [id://11111584|demo in the other answer] is Encode using "\x{FFFD}" to decode the broken character.

When it's reliable° in doing so, this could lead to better code.

Not sure what other multi-byte encodings are out there...

Cheers Rolf
(addicted to the Perl Programming Language :)
[id://1153804|Wikisyntax for the Monastery] FootballPerl is like chess, only without the dice

°) It is: from [doc://Encode] If CHECK is 0, encoding and decoding replace any malformed character with a substitution character. When you encode, SUBCHAR is used. When you decode, the Unicode REPLACEMENT CHARACTER, code point U+FFFD, is used. If the data is supposed to be UTF-8, an optional lexical warning of warning category "utf8" is given.

update

The Flag [https://perldoc.perl.org/Encode.html#List-of-_CHECK_-values|FB_QUIET seems to be the answer]
